question: Why can a composite wastewater sample be useful for evaluating a treatment plant's performance?
options: It combines aliquots collected over a sampling period, helping the sample represent changing wastewater conditions over time.
It measures every pollutant without laboratory analysis, so operators can use it instead of approved analytical methods.
It is always taken as one instantaneous grab, which makes it the best way to identify a short-term spill event.
It removes suspended solids before laboratory analysis, allowing a wastewater facility to skip required mixing and preservation steps.
explanation: Ontario Procedure F-10-1 describes a composite sample as aliquots taken over the required sampling period and thoroughly mixed. A composite can therefore help represent conditions that vary during that period when the applicable sampling program calls for it.
sourceTitle: Ontario MECP — F-10-1 Procedures for Sampling and Analysis Requirements for Municipal and Private Sewage Treatment Works
sourceReference: Section 2.1 states that composite samples should ideally consist of flow-proportioned aliquots taken at least once per hour over the required sampling period and that all aliquots should be thoroughly mixed.
